items.title: Validate safe delivery of the expanded MCP surface
items.source: README: Azure Functions; deletion confirmation; auto-labeling; issue #20
items.scope: Release the implemented branch only after deployed authorization, readback and protocol gates pass. Existing local tests and selected local live reproductions are evidence, not deployed all-tool readiness.
items.criteria: All required validation children pass with sanitized evidence; SDK migration acceptance remains intact; no unsupported authentication combination is advertised as supported. Failed writes/readbacks and deletion completion are reconciled before release.

items.title: Prove caller-bound deletion confirmation on remote hosting

items.criteria: Decline/cancel/malformed/expired/replayed/cross-caller requests never delete; stale target changes require new review; successful confirmation deletes only its bound object; logs contain no tenant payloads or credentials.

items.criteria: Record actual policy/rule/simulation response shapes; completed unchanged simulation permits guarded activation; missing/changed evidence prevents it; verify readback and clean up disposable objects without claiming existing labels are reversed.

items.title: Define and implement trusted simulation state across workers
items.scope: Design shared trusted state or explicitly constrain supported deployments to one process. Bind simulation evidence to caller, tenant, configuration and completion; no fabricated human approval.
items.criteria: A restarted/different worker cannot enable from untrusted evidence; chosen supported topology is documented and tested; expiry, invalidation and concurrent-change limits are defined. This gates a multi-worker activation claim, not single-process UAT.

items.title: Complete verified label and DLP control coverage
items.scope: Extend existing operations where parameter boundaries fit; keep new tool families tied to distinct objects. Core label/DLP CRUD and auto-label CRUD already exist.
items.criteria: Required stories pass local contracts and live readback; unsupported mappings fail explicitly; new surfaces have verified documentation and least-privilege authorization. Future suggestions remain refinement scope until their constraints are checked.

items.title: Apply advanced automatic-label controls with explicit support limits
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to configure supported advanced automatic-label rules, so that business targeting and matching requirements can be represented without silently weakening protection. Includes advanced expressions, multi-group matching, adaptive scopes, removal/library-default behavior, scheduled activation, overwrite, EDM/classifier and header/document-creator encodings; each is a separately verified slice, not a claim that all are currently supported.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Verified option
  Given a supported workload and eligible label
  When I submit a verified advanced configuration
  Then readback represents the requested control
Scenario: Unverified option
  Given an option whose mapping or authorization is unverified
  When I submit that option
  Then the request fails explicitly without mutation

items.title: Verify and implement advanced auto-label mappings incrementally
items.scope: Produce a parameter/workload/version matrix and split independently testable slices before implementation; preserve the ten-tool policy/rule architecture unless a distinct object requires more. Include empty-list clearing and enabled semantics; internal-only rule priority remains excluded.
items.criteria: Every enabled field has official mapping plus live readback; unsupported fields retain explicit rejection. Scheduled activation includes reviewed authorization and cancellation; classifier enumeration feasibility is separate from rule references.

items.title: Express remaining DLP conditions and exceptions
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to specify richer positive conditions and exceptions, so that legitimate transfers can be distinguished from prohibited ones. Includes non-Copilot label conditions and verified remaining ExceptIf fields; existing SIT tuning and common exceptions are implemented.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Matched condition
  Given a supported condition and workload
  When I save the rule
  Then readback preserves its matching and exception settings
Scenario: Unsupported combination
  Given an incompatible condition combination
  When I save the rule
  Then validation rejects it before mutation

items.title: Map richer DLP predicates and workload compatibility
items.scope: Define typed positive/exception schemas; verify Boolean encoding and workload restrictions. Do not expose arbitrary executable PowerShell or unchecked AdvancedRule payloads.
items.criteria: Tests cover mapping, mixed-condition boundaries, clearing/replacement semantics, permission checks and live readback; existing Copilot SIT/label mutual exclusion is preserved.

items.title: Configure remaining DLP remediation and incident reporting
items.source: ROADMAP: encrypt/RMS, quarantine, incident report; August F4
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to select supported remediation and incident-report settings, so that detected violations receive the required response and reporting. Incident-report recipients/content are distinct from alert recipients.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Incident reporting
  Given a supported rule and recipients
  When I save reporting settings
  Then readback contains GenerateIncidentReport and IncidentReportContent
Scenario: Unsupported action
  Given an action unavailable to the selected workload
  When I configure that action
  Then the request fails without changing the rule

items.title: Add incident-report recipients and content parameters
items.scope: Add parameters to existing create_dlp_rule/set_dlp_rule; retain current read fields and existing notifications.
items.criteria: Map GenerateIncidentReport and IncidentReportContent; validate accepted values/recipients and update semantics; prove tenant readback. No extra tool for a setting.

items.title: Verify encryption, quarantine and specialized endpoint actions
items.scope: Discover and implement verified encrypt/RMS, quarantine, on-premises scanner restrictions and UnallowedApps shapes as separable parameter slices.
items.criteria: Each action has documented workload support and typed shape; invalid mixtures reject before execution; live readback and action limitations are documented.

items.title: Target additional DLP workloads and administrative units
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to target supported additional workloads and administrative units, so that controls apply to the intended organizational boundary. Existing SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams/Endpoint exceptions are implemented.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Supported target
  Given a verified location surface or administrative unit
  When I save the policy scope
  Then readback contains that scope and preserves omitted fields
Scenario: Unverified target
  Given an unverified location type
  When I select that target
  Then the request is rejected without broader implicit scope

items.title: Verify remaining DLP locations and policy admin-unit parameters
items.source: ROADMAP: on-prem scanner, PowerBI, third-party apps, adaptive scopes; August F12 recommendation
items.scope: Confirm each location/API and map create/update/exclusion semantics. Administrative units on publishing and DLP policies are recommended refinement, distinct from implemented auto-label units.
items.criteria: Explicit per-workload surface matrix; verified PolicyRBACScopes exposure where supported; static/adaptive differences and RBAC tested; unsupported targets remain unavailable.

items.title: Refine publishing-policy ordering parameters
items.source: August F9 recommendation; label policy setters
items.scope: Proposed extension: next_label_policy/previous_label_policy on set_label_policy, after verifying mutual exclusion and backend behavior. This recommendation is not yet implementation.
items.criteria: Resolve the referenced policy; reject conflicting position requests; map NextLabelPolicy/PreviousLabelPolicy; verify resulting relative order by live readback.

items.title: Author and inspect reusable classification primitives
items.source: ROADMAP: keyword dictionaries; SIT packages; custom SIT XML; EDM
items.scope: Provide dictionary, SIT rule-package and EDM schema capabilities with validated data formats and identity-safe updates.
items.criteria: Read/export and each authoring story passes format checks, permission tests and live readback; original XML constraints are verified rather than assumed; package removal and dependent controls are reviewed safely.

items.title: Manage keyword dictionaries for classification
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to manage keyword dictionaries, so that reusable large keyword sets can support classification rules.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Dictionary update
  Given a supported dictionary and valid terms
  When I create or update its contents
  Then readback contains the intended terms
Scenario: Invalid input
  Given terms outside confirmed limits
  When I submit the dictionary
  Then validation rejects the request without mutation

items.title: Implement verified keyword dictionary operations
items.scope: Verify read/create/set/remove semantics, term encoding and limits; choose object-specific capabilities and deletion guard integration.
items.criteria: Canonical identity, pagination where needed, format boundaries, protected parameter passing and tenant CRUD readback are covered.

items.title: Inspect and safely author custom sensitive information types
items.source: ROADMAP: SIT rule-package read; Custom SIT write; August F6
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to inspect and author custom SIT packages, so that organization-specific identifiers can be detected without malformed package uploads. Structured authoring and validated caller-supplied XML are distinct supported input paths.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Valid package
  Given a validated package specification
  When I submit the package
  Then export/readback contains the intended SIT definitions
Scenario: Invalid package
  Given malformed or unsupported XML
  When I submit the package
  Then local validation rejects it before upload

items.title: Add SIT rule-package read and export
items.scope: Implement safe package catalogue/detail/export, selecting a tool/resource contract without returning unbounded XML by default.
items.criteria: Built-in/custom identity distinctions, byte encoding and permission behavior verified; export is suitable for a subsequent version-aware update.

items.title: Build validated custom SIT package create/update/remove
items.scope: Confirm regex restrictions, confidence/validator schema, Unicode encoding, package-size limits and dictionary rules (historical roadmap mentions 2048 terms/50-character terms/~770 KB; verify actual current limits). Updates export, mutate and reimport; preserve package IDs and existing definitions.
items.criteria: Structured authoring and validated XML import reject malformed/oversized/unsupported packages; stale export changes detected; live create/update/remove/readback works; dependency/removal consequences surfaced.

items.title: Manage exact-data-match schemas safely
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to manage EDM schemas, so that exact-match classifications use an explicit validated schema. Data upload or ingestion pipelines require separate scoping and are not silently included.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Valid schema
  Given a supported EDM schema definition
  When I create or update it
  Then readback contains its intended fields and identities
Scenario: Invalid schema
  Given malformed or incompatible schema XML
  When I submit it
  Then validation rejects it without mutation

items.title: Verify and implement EDM schema XML lifecycle
items.scope: Verify XML constraints and Get/New/Set/Remove cmdlet availability; provide validated byte conversion and reviewed deletion.
items.criteria: Schema identity, update semantics, malformed input, RBAC and live lifecycle are proven; data ingestion remains explicitly outside this schema-only slice.

items.title: Review DLP detections and report evidence
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to retrieve supported detection reports, so that control reviews can distinguish configuration from observed detections. Configuration presence alone is not enforcement proof.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Report retrieval
  Given authorized access and an explicit report range
  When I request a supported report
  Then the result identifies its source, range and available evidence
Scenario: Missing access
  Given insufficient report permissions
  When I request the report
  Then access failure is explicit rather than reported as zero detections

items.title: Validate DLP report surfaces and bounded read contracts
items.scope: Confirm current cmdlet availability, license/role requirements, retention windows, pagination and alert/report distinctions before implementation.
items.criteria: Bounded authorized retrieval and sensitive-content handling tested; unsupported or retired report surfaces documented without inventing empty results.

items.title: Extend protection to verified enterprise AI surfaces
items.source: ROADMAP: AI DLP Application; FeatureConfiguration capture
items.scope: Add enterprise AI Application-plane configuration and separately scoped prompt/response capture. Existing Microsoft 365 Copilot phase-one tools are implemented.
items.criteria: Application and capture children meet verified API/auth constraints; deprecated Entra plane is not used; application integration and data-collection privacy remain explicit boundaries.

items.title: Configure DLP for Entra-registered enterprise AI applications
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to scope DLP to registered AI applications, so that sensitive prompts can be restricted through the supported Application enforcement plane. The application developer remains responsible for integrating processContent.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Application policy
  Given a verified registered application and supported predicates
  When I configure its DLP rule
  Then readback contains its application location and restriction
Scenario: Unsupported plane
  Given the deprecated Entra enforcement-plane value
  When I select that value
  Then validation rejects it

items.title: Build verified Application Locations and AdvancedRule encoding
items.scope: Confirm official JSON schemas and workload/action combinations; map Application not deprecated Entra; test RestrictAccess/RestrictWebGrounding only where supported. Discover external-email Copilot grounding preview separately.
items.criteria: Typed builders, supported combinations, permission boundaries and live readback verified; processContent application implementation is documented as excluded.

items.title: Configure reviewed AI prompt and response collection
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to configure authorized AI collection policies, so that approved investigations have the intended collection scope. This is a separate configuration family, not a side effect of DLP creation.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Reviewed collection scope
  Given an explicitly approved collection configuration
  When I save the policy
  Then readback identifies its intended collection scope
Scenario: Invalid scenario
  Given an unsupported ScenarioConfig
  When I submit it
  Then the request fails without creating a collection policy

items.title: Verify FeatureConfiguration lifecycle and ScenarioConfig
items.scope: Verify cmdlets, JSON schema, licensing, RBAC and information-handling constraints before exposing reviewed CRUD operations.
items.criteria: Typed validation and live readback/removal proven; collection limits and retention/privacy implications documented; no automatic enabling from an assessment.

items.title: Establish a coherent retention-label and policy solution
items.scope: Build the retention read model before writes; cover actions, review stages and adaptive scopes as verified slices.
items.criteria: Read-first model and safe write story pass authorized live lifecycle; irreversible or restricted changes are explicit; retention is not conflated with sensitivity labels.

items.title: Inspect and configure supported retention controls
items.scope: As a Purview administrator, I want to inspect and configure retention controls, so that records follow the intended lifecycle rather than a sensitivity-label policy.
items.criteria:
Scenario: Read retention state
  Given authorized access to retention configuration
  When I inspect a retention label or policy
  Then the result identifies its action, scope and review settings
Scenario: Unsupported change
  Given an immutable or unsupported retention change
  When I submit that change
  Then it is rejected before mutation
